title: The Thunderstorm
intro: Thunder rumbles over the building. Aarav loves storms, but his sister Diya hides under a blanket.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: Aarav and Diya feel the same way about the storm.
Two people can feel differently about the same thing.
Diya is scared of the storm.
Aarav hides under a blanket.

sections.title: Who would say it? Sort.
words: Let us watch from the window

sections.title: Circle the correct word.
The same rain, different feelings. Match.

items.right: is happy because the crops get water.

items.left: The child with a new kite
items.right: is sad because kites cannot fly in rain.
is happy because the pond fills up.
is upset because the washing gets wet.

sections.title: What do you think about storms? Write: I think ... because ...
sections.a: e.g. I think storms are exciting because the sky lights up.

title: Broccoli for Dinner
intro: Mum has cooked broccoli tonight. Hana smiles, but her brother Yusuf makes a face.

sections.title: Fill in each blank with but or because.

items.q: Hana thinks broccoli is tasty, ___ Yusuf thinks it is yucky.
Hana likes it ___ it is crunchy.
Yusuf does not like it ___ it smells strong.
Mum likes broccoli, ___ Dad likes carrots more.

sections.title: Match each point of view to its reason.

items.left: Leo thinks mangoes are the best fruit
items.right: because they are sweet and juicy.
because they are so sour.

items.left: Ken thinks chillies are too much
items.right: because they burn his tongue.

items.left: Asha thinks ice cream is perfect
items.right: because it is cold on a hot day.

sections.title: Does the speaker like the food or not? Sort.
Circle True or False.

items.q: Everyone must like the same food.
Yusuf thinks broccoli is yucky.
It is fine for Hana and Yusuf to think differently.
The word 'because' helps us give a reason.

sections.title: Write about a food you like. Use: I think ... because ...

items.q: My food:
items.a: e.g. I think dal is tasty because it is warm and soft.

title: The Cat and the Mouse
intro: A cat sits by a small hole in the wall. Inside the hole, a mouse is watching. They see the same room very differently.

sections.title: Who is thinking it? Sort.
words: That hole is too small for me

sections.title: How does each one see it? Match.

items.right: is a scary giant.
is something to chase.

items.left: A bowl of milk, to a cat,
items.right: is a tasty treat.

items.left: A tiny hole, to a mouse,
items.right: is a safe home.

items.left: A barking dog, to a cat,
items.right: is a reason to run up a tree.

sections.title: Circle the correct word.

items.after: the mouse is fun to chase.

items.before: The mouse thinks the cat is
The mouse stays in its hole

sections.title: Write the feeling. Use: scared, safe, bored.

items.q: The mouse feels ___ when the cat comes near.
Deep inside its hole, the mouse feels ___.
The cat feels ___ when nothing happens for an hour.

sections.title: Pretend you are the mouse. Write two sentences about the cat.
sections.a: e.g. I think the cat is scary because it has sharp claws. I will stay in my hole until it goes away.

title: The Swimming Pool
intro: It is the first swimming lesson. Nora jumps right in, Jai dips one toe, and Coach Peter watches them both.

sections.title: Match each person to their point of view.

items.right: The water is fun. I want to dive!
The water looks deep. I will go slowly.
Everyone must stay safe in my class.
I hope my son enjoys his lesson.

sections.title: Write think or thinks.

items.q: Nora ___ swimming is the best sport.
I ___ the pool is cold today.
Jai and his mum ___ the deep end is scary.
Coach Peter ___ every child can learn to swim.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: Nora and Jai feel the same about the water.
Jai is wrong to feel nervous.
Different feelings about one thing can both be okay.
Nora is excited about swimming.

sections.title: Write the opposite word. Use: boring, hard, noisy, dangerous.

items.q: fun
easy
quiet
safe

sections.title: Join the two sentences with but.

items.q: Nora thinks the pool is fun. Jai thinks it is scary.
items.a: Nora thinks the pool is fun, but Jai thinks it is scary.

sections.title: What do you think about swimming? Give a reason.
sections.a: e.g. I think swimming is fun because I can splash and float.

title: A Loud Fireworks Night
intro: Fireworks light up the sky over the Corniche. The crowd claps, a baby cries and a dog hides under a bench.

sections.title: Match each one to how they see the fireworks.

items.right: They are bright and beautiful!
That bang woke me up!
The noise hurts my ears. I must hide.
I worked hard to make this show.

sections.title: Circle the best joining word.

items.before: Grandpa thinks the show is too long,
items.after: Mira thinks it is too short.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: The dog and the children feel the same about fireworks.
A loud sound can be fun for one person and scary for another.
The firework maker worked hard to make the show.
The baby enjoys the loud bangs.

sections.title: Write both views in one sentence. Use thinks ... but ... thinks.

items.q: Mira: Fireworks are pretty. Grandpa: Fireworks are noisy.
items.a: e.g. Mira thinks fireworks are pretty, but Grandpa thinks they are noisy.

items.q: The dog: Bangs are scary. Mira: Bangs are exciting.
items.a: e.g. The dog thinks bangs are scary, but Mira thinks they are exciting.

sections.title: Do you like fireworks? Write what you think and give a reason.
sections.a: e.g. I think fireworks are lovely because they look like flowers in the sky.

title: The Neighbour's Dog
intro: Bruno is a big, friendly dog who lives next door. Not everyone on the street feels the same about him.

sections.title: Does the speaker like Bruno or not? Sort.
Complete each sentence. Use: thinks, think, but, because.

items.q: Tara ___ Bruno is gentle.
The twins ___ Bruno is too noisy.
Mr Rao likes dogs, ___ he does not like barking at night.
Baby Zain cries ___ Bruno's bark is loud.

sections.title: Match each neighbour to a reason.

items.right: because he plays fetch with her.

items.left: Mr Rao is cross with Bruno
items.right: because he dug up the rose bed.
because Bruno runs to the gate barking.
because Bruno scares away thieves.

items.left: The cat stays on the wall
items.right: because Bruno chases her.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: All the neighbours think the same about Bruno.
Tara and Mr Rao have different points of view.
A point of view is how someone thinks or feels about something.

sections.title: Pretend you are Bruno. What do you think about the postman? Give a reason.
sections.a: e.g. I think the postman is a stranger because he comes to my gate every day.

title: Homework on Saturday
intro: Miss Fernandes gave the class a page of sums for the weekend. Listen to what everyone thinks.

sections.title: Match each person to their point of view.

items.right: Practice helps children learn.
Saturday is for cricket, not sums!
I like sums. This will be fun.
Finish it early, then go and play.

sections.title: Circle think or thinks.
Finish each reason. Use: learn, play, proud, tired.

items.q: Miss Fernandes gives homework because she wants us to ___.
Arjun is grumpy because he wants to ___ outside.
Sofia is happy because a page full of ticks makes her feel ___.
Dad says start early because at night you will be too ___.

sections.title: Join the two sentences with but.

items.q: Sofia thinks homework is fun. Arjun thinks it is boring.
items.a: Sofia thinks homework is fun, but Arjun thinks it is boring.

items.q: Dad wants the sums done first. Arjun wants to play first.
items.a: Dad wants the sums done first, but Arjun wants to play first.

sections.title: What do you think about weekend homework? Give a reason with because.
sections.a: e.g. I think a little homework is fine because it helps me remember my tables.

title: The Roller Coaster at the Fair
intro: The Dragon Loop is the tallest ride at the fair. Four cousins stand in line, and each one feels something different.

sections.title: How does each speaker feel? Sort.
words: I have done this ten times
It is too high for me

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: One ride can give different people different feelings.
If you are scared of a ride, your feeling is wrong.
'I cannot wait!' shows an excited point of view.
Everyone in the line thinks the ride is boring.

sections.title: Write but or because.

items.q: Kiran wants to sit in front ___ he loves going fast.
Lucy wants to ride, ___ Bela wants to watch.
Bela holds Mum's hand ___ the ride looks very high.
The Dragon Loop is fast, ___ the Ferris wheel is slow.

sections.title: Match the start to the best ending.

items.left: Kiran thinks the loop is thrilling,
items.right: but Bela thinks it is terrifying.

items.left: Lucy thinks the queue is too long,
items.right: but Omkar thinks the wait is worth it.

items.left: Mum thinks candy floss is too sweet,
items.right: but the children think it is delicious.

items.left: Dad thinks the music is too loud,
items.right: but Lucy thinks it is perfect for dancing.

sections.title: Would you ride the Dragon Loop? Write: I think ... because ...
sections.a: e.g. I think the Dragon Loop is too scary because it goes upside down.

title: The Bird and the Worm
intro: It is early morning in the garden. A hungry bird hops on the grass, and a little worm wriggles in the soil.

sections.title: How does each animal see it? Match.

items.right: is lovely because the soil gets soft.
is a problem because wet wings cannot fly.

items.left: A tall tree, to a bird,
items.right: is a safe place for a nest.

items.left: A tall tree, to an ant,
items.right: is a very long climb.
is a scary stranger in the field.

sections.title: Who is thinking it? Sort.
words: I can see far from up here

sections.title: Circle the correct word.

items.before: The bird thinks the worm is
The worm thinks the bird is

items.after: morning is the best time to hunt.

sections.title: Write one sentence. Use: The bird thinks ... but the worm thinks ...

items.q: The garden: a place to find food, or a place to hide?
items.a: e.g. The bird thinks the garden is a place to find food, but the worm thinks it is a place to hide.

sections.title: Pretend you are the worm. Write two sentences about your morning.
sections.a: e.g. I think mornings are risky because birds are hungry. I stayed under a wet leaf until the bird flew away.

title: A Hot Summer Afternoon
intro: It is a very hot June afternoon in Dubai. Some people love the heat, and some cannot wait for winter.

sections.title: Complete each sentence. Use: thinks, think, but, because.

items.q: The ice cream seller ___ summer is wonderful.
The gardeners ___ the sun is too strong.
Pia loves summer ___ the pool is open.
Pia loves summer, ___ her cat hates the heat.

sections.title: Match each one to their point of view about summer.

items.right: Hot days bring me many customers.
My plants dry up too quickly.
No school for two months!
Heat does not bother me much.
Oh no, I will melt!

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: The ice cream seller and the gardener see summer differently.
A point of view can come with a reason.
'Summer is the best season' is true for everyone.
The gardener is happy that the plants dry up.

sections.title: Finish each sentence with your own reason.

items.q: I think summer is fun because
items.a: e.g. I think summer is fun because I can swim every day.

items.q: My friend thinks winter is better because
items.a: e.g. My friend thinks winter is better because we can play outside.

title: The Class Pet Spider
intro: Mr Haddad brought a pet spider called Velvet to Class 2. Now tell facts from opinions and give strong reasons.

sections.title: Fact or opinion? Sort.
words: Velvet lives in a glass tank

sections.title: Match each point of view to its reason.

items.right: because she spins such neat webs.
because her legs are long and hairy.

items.left: Mr Haddad thinks spiders are useful
items.right: because they eat flies and mosquitoes.

items.left: The fly thinks spiders are terrible
items.right: because webs are sticky traps.

sections.title: Circle the correct word.
Write both views in one sentence. Use but.

items.q: Ines: Velvet is cute. Rohit: Velvet is frightening.
items.a: e.g. Ines thinks Velvet is cute, but Rohit thinks she is frightening.

items.q: Mr Haddad: Spiders are useful. The fly: Spiders are terrible.
items.a: e.g. Mr Haddad thinks spiders are useful, but the fly thinks they are terrible.

sections.title: Should a class have a pet spider? Write what you think and give a reason.
sections.a: e.g. I think a class should have a pet spider because we can learn how it spins a web.

title: Bedtime at Eight O'Clock
intro: Mum says lights out at eight. Vihaan wants to stay up. Read both sides before you decide.

sections.title: Whose reason is it? Sort.
words: My book is at the best part

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: Mum and Vihaan both have reasons for what they think.
Vihaan thinks eight o'clock is too early.
Mum's reasons are about keeping Vihaan healthy and rested.
A fair person listens to only one point of view.

sections.title: Complete each sentence. Use: thinks, but, because, so.

items.q: Mum ___ sleep is more important than stories.
Vihaan feels wide awake, ___ Mum says it is bedtime.
Mum sets an early bedtime ___ school starts at seven.
Mum let Vihaan read for ten minutes, ___ both of them were happy.

sections.title: Now write the other person's point of view.

items.q: Vihaan: I think bedtime should be at nine because I am not tired.
items.a: e.g. Mum thinks bedtime should be at eight because Vihaan has school early.

items.q: Mum: I think screens should be off after dinner.
items.a: e.g. Vihaan thinks one cartoon after dinner is fine because it helps him relax.

sections.title: What is a fair bedtime for a seven-year-old? Give your view and a reason.
sections.a: e.g. I think half past eight is fair because children need ten hours of sleep.

title: The Farmer and the Monkeys
intro: A troop of monkeys visits a banana farm in Kerala every morning. The farmer and the monkeys do not see it the same way.

sections.title: Match each start to the right point of view.

items.left: To the farmer, the bananas are
items.right: fruit to sell at the market.

items.left: To the monkeys, the bananas are
items.right: a free breakfast.

items.left: To the farmer, the monkeys are
items.right: naughty thieves.

items.left: To the monkeys, the farmer is
items.right: a noisy man with a stick.

items.left: To the farmer's son, the monkeys are
items.right: funny acrobats to watch.

sections.title: Circle the correct word.

items.after: when the monkeys take his fruit.

items.before: The monkeys come to the farm

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: The farmer and the monkeys see the bananas in the same way.
The monkeys take bananas because they need food.
The farmer grows bananas to sell them.
Looking at both sides helps us understand a problem.

sections.title: Write what the smallest monkey thinks about the farmer. Use because.

items.q: The smallest monkey says:
items.a: e.g. I think the farmer is scary because he shouts and waves a stick.

sections.title: How could the farmer and the monkeys both be happy? Write your idea.
sections.a: e.g. The farmer could plant a few banana trees near the forest for the monkeys. Then the monkeys would not need to come to the farm.

title: Sharing a Room
intro: Sisters Anika and Rhea share one bedroom. Anika likes it neat and quiet. Rhea likes music and a floor full of toys.

sections.title: Who would say it? Sort.
words: Let us dance on the bed

sections.title: Write the opposite word. Use: messy, noisy, late, wild.

items.q: neat
quiet
early
calm

sections.title: Match each wish to its reason.

items.right: because she tripped on a toy car.

items.left: Rhea wants her blocks left out
items.right: because her tower is not finished.

items.left: Anika wants the light off early
items.right: because she wakes up at six.

items.left: Rhea wants the night lamp on
items.right: because she dislikes the dark.

sections.title: Circle True or False.

items.q: Anika and Rhea want the same kind of room.
Each sister has reasons for what she wants.
Listening to each other can help the sisters agree.

sections.title: Write both views in one sentence. Use thinks ... but ... thinks.

items.q: Anika: The music is too loud. Rhea: The music is just right.
items.a: e.g. Anika thinks the music is too loud, but Rhea thinks it is just right.

sections.title: Write a room rule that is fair to both sisters. Say why.
sections.a: e.g. Toys can stay out until dinner and then go in the box. This is fair because Rhea can play and Anika gets a clear floor at night.

title: A New Playground Rule
intro: The principal says only Classes 1 and 2 may use the swings at first break. Find out what everyone thinks, then give your own view.

sections.title: Match each person to their point of view.

items.right: Small children need a safe turn.
Hooray, no more long waits!
That is unfair. We like swings too.
Fewer children at once means fewer falls.

sections.title: Fact or opinion? Sort.
words: First break is at ten o'clock

sections.title: Circle the correct word.

items.before: A Class 5 child thinks the rule is unfair

items.after: the rule keeps little ones safe.

items.before: The rule is good for Class 2,
'I think' tells the listener it is my

sections.title: Write the two views in one sentence. Use but.

items.q: Class 2: The rule is great. Class 5: The rule is unfair.
items.a: e.g. Class 2 thinks the rule is great, but Class 5 thinks it is unfair.

sections.title: What do you think of the rule? Write: I think ... because ... Then add what someone else may think.
sections.a: e.g. I think the rule is fair because small children get pushed. A Class 5 child may think it is unfair because they love swings too.
